key_insight: Instead of re-deriving the same control logic inside every LLM task prompt, the paper shows that recurring agent decisions can be converted into reusable executable harness code. This lets the model focus on task-specific reasoning while the harness handles repeated strategy.
problem_solved: LLM agents often waste context and computation by repeatedly reconstructing the same control decisions for related tasks. The paper addresses how to make agent behavior more efficient and reusable across a stream of tasks.
method: Use a strategy-free scaffold that exposes failures without hard-coding task strategy.
Apply feedback-driven training to grow the harness into executable code that captures recurring control decisions.
Reserve LLM calls for semantic, task-specific reasoning instead of repeated orchestration logic.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this can reduce context bloat, improve reuse across task sequences, and make agents more efficient and modular. It suggests a practical path from prompt-heavy agent scaffolds to more reliable specialist systems.
visual_elements: Before/after diagram comparing a standard prompt-heavy agent versus a reusable harness-based agent
Flowchart showing task feedback being converted into harness code
Stacked architecture graphic separating reusable control logic from task-specific LLM reasoning
Icon set for failures, feedback loops, code generation, and agent execution
paper_title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
paper_authors: Laizhen Li, Jiarui Li, Juanjuan Zhao, Kejiang Ye, Ye Li
